notes: Focused v1.9.0 content-and-structure regressions (#73 so far: layout sketches at the floor size, the States section, concrete defaults, the clutter-audit example, palette and `/` guidance). Later v1.9.0 issues add cases here. Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash. Status (2026-10-27): recorded. Baseline and with-skill runs on Claude Code and Codex, three repetitions per case, are in evals/results/v1.9.0-claude-comparison/ and evals/results/v1.9.0-codex-comparison/ against skill tree 164c1aefd956.

evals.name: floor-sketch-layout
evals.prompt: I'm building a TUI for browsing Kubernetes pods: a namespace sidebar, a pod list, and a detail pane with logs. Design the layout for me.
assertions: Recommends a layout shape (for example IDE-style panes or a drill-down stack) before explaining it
Includes an ASCII sketch of the wide layout and an ASCII sketch at 60 columns or the 80x24 floor
Shows what folds away at the narrow size (for example the detail pane first, then the sidebar) and that a single-pane fallback exists
Names a minimum size below which the app shows a 'terminal too small' state that states the dimensions it needs
Draws the sketches with ASCII or narrow-width characters, or names an ASCII fallback for box drawing

evals.name: state-coverage
evals.prompt: Review the screens of my release-dashboard TUI. It fetches build status from five CI servers, and I only designed the happy path. What states does it need?
assertions: Lists the states beyond the happy path: initial, loading, empty, partial, error, disconnected or stale, and too small
Describes partial as showing what loaded while marking the failed sources inline (for example '4 of 5 servers') with a retry action, rather than blanking the screen or hiding the failure
Says a stale or disconnected view keeps the last-known-good data visible, dimmed, with an age or 'stale' marker
Gives every state a next action (retry, cancel, change scope) instead of a bare message
Does not rely on color alone to distinguish the states

evals.name: clutter-audit-counts
evals.prompt: This feels busy. Each row of my test list looks like `> [PASS] (ok) build 2.1s`, and the whole list is inside two nested bordered boxes. How do I clean it up?
assertions: Counts offenders instead of saying 'simplify': border-nesting depth, signals per status, and the always-on `>` marker
Reports that the status is encoded more than once (tag, `(ok)`, and color) and keeps at most one color cue plus one non-color cue
Removes the always-on row marker, reserving a marker or reverse video for the selected row
Removes the nested borders so at most one border sits between the terminal edge and the content, or none
Mentions the share of cells spent on chrome versus data

evals.name: status-message-timing
evals.prompt: How long should status-line messages stay on screen in my TUI, and what should happen to errors?
assertions: Says success and info messages fade after about 3-5 seconds
Says errors and warnings stay until the user dismisses them
Says dismissed errors move to a message log the user can reopen
Leads messages with a symbol or label word so the kind survives NO_COLOR

evals.name: footer-hint-collapse
evals.prompt: Design the footer hint bar for my file-manager TUI. It has about eight actions. Show what it looks like at 80 columns and at 40.
assertions: Shows one rendered footer line at 80 columns and a shorter line at 40 columns
Orders hints by frequency of use with the most frequent first
Keeps `?` for help as the last hint at both widths so the full list stays one key away
Drops the least frequent hints first as width shrinks
Uses a narrow-width separator such as `⋅` or `|` rather than an ambiguous-width middle dot, or names the risk

evals.name: palette-and-slash
evals.prompt: My log viewer has about 35 actions across several screens. Should I add a command palette, and what should `/` do?
assertions: Recommends a command palette because the app is past roughly 20 actions and its actions span several contexts
Says every keybound action should also be a palette command, with its key shown beside it
Says `/` searches in documents and logs, with Enter jumping to the first match and n/N cycling, and filters in lists
Warns that Ctrl+P can be captured (Zellij, readline) and offers `:` or a leader key as an alternative
